name: Gishpa
overview: Gishpa is a male descendant of the tribe of Levi, known for his leadership role in overseeing the temple servants. His responsibility highlights a position of trust and service within the Levitical duties related to the temple. Scripture specifically notes his charge over these temple workers, emphasizing his role in the religious community.
namesAndTitles: The name Gishpa means 'listener,' which is a proper name recorded in Nehemiah 11:21. This name does not appear to be given directly by God but reflects a meaningful Hebrew term associated with attentiveness.
familyAndRelationships: Gishpa is explicitly identified as a descendant of Levi, establishing his place within the Levitical lineage. Beyond this tribal relationship, Scripture does not record additional family connections for him.
scriptureSignificance: Gishpa's significance lies in his leadership among the temple servants, an important aspect of maintaining the worship and service in the post-exilic community. His role exemplifies faithful stewardship and dedication to God's house, rooted in his Levitical heritage. By managing temple servants, Gishpa contributed to the orderly function of worship, reflecting the ongoing commitment of the Levites to God's covenant.
